whyV2Exists: Every figure measured on v1 has been WITHDRAWN. Two independent instrument defects, not a tuning disagreement.

Defect A (NV-REQID-CORRELATION-001, since FIXED): the requestId returned to the caller was not the id used at LLM dispatch, so provider log lines could not be joined to a request. The harness silently fell back to scopeMode:'window' and counted every billed line in a TIME WINDOW, which on a shared dev host attributes other concurrent requests to the request under test. The widely-repeated v1 finding that single-issue-advice billed '3 completions' was an artefact of that: request-scoped fan-out is 1.

Defect B (this file's subject): set composition. 30% of v1's blended weight was trivial statute lookups that score a free 100% and pad the blend; and all 7 cost-bearing prompts were the SAME topic (anticipatory bail / BNSS 482), so the semantic cache cross-hit between them. v1's zero-completion results on legal-research / multi-issue-strategy / drafting were cache false positives manufactured by the set's own monotopicity, not savings.
whatThisSetCanProve: Per-class MEASURED token counts, billed completion counts and USD cost for the NYV orchestrated path against a real direct provider call on the same model, with each figure joinable to one requestId.
Variance across DISTINCT INPUTS within a class: 3 independent prompts per cost-bearing class, so a per-class spread is a real sample spread and not the cold/warm artefact of repeating one prompt.

Whether a zero-cost answer was earned: every zero-completion run carries a STATED mechanism (cost.resolution, NV-ZEROCOST-ATTRIBUTION-001) so a cache hit, a deterministic answer and an out-of-scope fast path are separable rather than collapsed into one count.
Whether the trivial-lookup classes still resolve deterministically, reported on their own line and never folded into the headline.
Whether the set's own topic separation held on the pass: a cold run that reports resolution 'semantic-cache' VOIDS the pass (see cacheIsolation.runtimeSelfTest).
whatThisSetCannotProve: A blended cost figure representative of real traffic. The class weights are ASSUMED (see weighting.provenance). No sampled traffic mix exists anywhere in this repository — the only asset that could yield one is nv_router_decisions.task_kind, and nothing has ever aggregated it.

LEGAL CORRECTNESS. Nothing here is a legal-quality score. Keyword/citation containment makes a cost win from silently answering less visible; it cannot tell a right answer from a plausible wrong one. Raw answers exist for SME scoring and that scoring has not been done.

That a cached answer is the RIGHT answer. Attribution proves the mechanism was a cache hit; only content scoring can prove the cached text answers THIS prompt. The cross-prompt duplicate check catches the crude case (byte-identical to another item's answer) and nothing weaker.

Embedding-space separation of the prompts. Separation is verified structurally and lexically offline (see separation.method); the live gate is cosine similarity of provider embeddings, which cannot be computed without the embedding provider. The runtime self-test is what actually closes this gap, after the fact.

Anything under concurrency, streaming, or with a genuinely large attached document. Runs are serial and non-streamed; the long-context items are ~400-word fact matrices, which is a longer prompt and not a long document. Nothing here measures a 40-page brief.
Cost of non-LLM infrastructure (RAG embeddings, NYS round trips, DB). §12.1 measured 236s of a 366s Queen request as non-LLM time; that time has a real cost this set does not price.
_meta.publicationRule: No cost-reduction percentage may be published from any pass of this set until (a) the metering verdict is 'ok' with scopeMode 'requestId' on every row, (b) every zero-cost run is attributed with signal 'envelope' or 'log' (no 'unattributable'), (c) the weights are replaced with sampled traffic, and (d) an SME has scored the answers. Conditions (c) and (d) are NOT met today.

baseline.rationale: The claim is 'NYV vs calling the model directly', so the baseline must be a real provider call. The SAME model the NYV router actually selects is used, so answer quality is equivalent by construction and any measured delta is attributable to orchestration rather than to a cheaper model.
baseline.systemInstructionNote: Deliberately none. 'Direct LLM' means the user's prompt with no scaffolding — that IS the alternative being compared against. A system prompt would make the baseline more expensive and flatter NYV.
baseline.notCoveredNote: A single direct call is not like-for-like against a naive integration that also retries or hedges. Where a real integration would, the baseline understates direct cost, i.e. this comparison is conservative against NYV.

weighting.honestCaveat: These shares are an ASSUMPTION, unchanged in kind from v1. A blended cost figure is only as good as this table, and no sampled traffic exists in this repository to replace it with. The candidate source is nv_router_decisions.task_kind, which is populated but has never been aggregated. Until a dated aggregation over a stated window is committed, treat every blended figure from this set as conditional on a mix nobody has measured.
weighting.provenance: ASSUMED. Traced to the share_of_traffic column of the TODAY table in scripts/nv-cost-model.py (lines 29-34), which is hand-authored. That file's header says 'Measured today' — that claim covers the token and wall-clock columns only; the share column is not measured and no comment in the file says where it came from.
weighting.evidenceSearchPerformed: Searched docs/, docs/audit/, documents/working/, .local/benchmarks/, every CSV and audit JSON, and every scripts/*usage*|*traffic*|*mix* file for a sampled request-class distribution. None exists.
whatWouldMakeTheseDerived: nv_router_decisions carries task_kind (shared/schema.ts nvRouterDecisions; DDL migrations/2026-05-28-legal-doc-domain-catchup.sql; written by src/services/intelligent-router/router-stats.ts). Nothing in the repo has ever GROUPed BY it — grep for 'GROUP BY task_kind' returns zero matches, and there is no index on the column.
nv_usage_logs is aggregated by agent_key in nv-gateway-routes.ts, which is a proxy for agent selection, not for request class.
Until a dated aggregation of nv_router_decisions.task_kind over a stated window is committed as an artifact, every weight below stays 'assumed'.
weighting.headlineRule: The headline blend covers COST-BEARING classes only and renormalises their mixShare to 1.0 among themselves (sum of cost-bearing mixShare = 0.70). The trivial-lookup classes are reported on their own line with their own figures and are NEVER added to the headline. In v1 they contributed 0.30 of blended weight at a free 100% saving, which is 30 points of headline handed over by the set's own composition.
weighting.fullMixFigureIsSecondary: A full-mix figure including the trivial classes may be computed and printed, clearly labelled as such, so the size of the padding is visible instead of hidden.
weighting.reallocationNote: §1.0's 'classify/extract' 0.10 has no counterpart class here and is reallocated to multi-issue-strategy 0.05, multi-jurisdiction-conflict 0.03, long-context 0.02 — the same reallocation v1 made. It is an assumption layered on an assumption and is called out so a re-blend against a different mix is possible without editing prompts.

separation.requirement: No two cost-bearing prompts may be close enough for the semantic cache to serve one's answer for the other.

liveGateAsBuilt.servedAt: cosine >= semanticServeThreshold, default 0.94 (env NYV_LMCACHE_SEMANTIC_SERVE_MIN) — src/services/lm-cache-service.ts findSemanticMatch
liveGateAsBuilt.countedNeverServed: 0.88 <= cosine < 0.94 is the grounding band: counted as semanticNearMisses, never served
liveGateAsBuilt.correctionToPriorBriefings: LMCacheConfig.similarityThreshold = 0.85 is DECLARED AND SET BUT NEVER READ — grep for config.similarityThreshold in src/ returns no reader. The 0.85 figure repeated in earlier write-ups is dead config. The gate that actually serves is 0.94.
liveGateAsBuilt.additionalPrecondition: Fuzzy matching only runs in a tenant-attributable namespace (isFuzzyMatchSafeNamespace, src/services/nv-lm-cache-key.ts). A namespace resolving to specialist:anon:... is excluded, so on an unauthenticated or tenant-less call semantic matching is OFF and cross-hits are impossible for a reason unrelated to topic distance. A pass must record which case applied.
liveGateAsBuilt.exactKeyMatch: Separate path, not gated on the above: byte-identical normalised user turn within the same namespace and corpus version (buildCacheKeyParts). Distinct prompts cannot collide on it.

method: 1. STRUCTURAL, by construction. Every cost-bearing prompt is assigned a topicAnchors set naming its instrument(s), forum and subject matter. The set asserts that no two cost-bearing prompts share ANY anchor. This is a hard, mechanically checkable property — see tests/unit/nv-benchmark-set-v2-separation.test.ts.

2. LEXICAL, using the production normaliser. Each prompt is passed through the real normalizeForCacheKey() from src/services/nv-lm-cache-key.ts (imported, not copied — NV-NO-DUPLICATE-001) and pairwise token-set cosine is computed. Ceiling asserted: 0.30. v1's cost-bearing prompts are run through the same check as a control and must FAIL it, so the check is proven to have teeth rather than being a formality that everything passes.
3. RUNTIME SELF-TEST, the only one that touches the actual gate. See cacheIsolation.runtimeSelfTest.
separation.honestLimitOfMethod: Steps 1 and 2 are offline SCREENS, not proofs. The live gate is cosine similarity of provider embeddings (multilingual-e5-large / in-legal-bert / text-embedding-3-large per nv-legal-embedding-service.ts), which cannot be computed without reaching the embedding provider, and low lexical overlap does not entail low embedding cosine — two differently-worded questions about the same legal concept can embed close together. Step 3 is therefore not a nicety: it is what converts a screen into a measurement, after the fact, on the build under test.

measuredAtFreeze.maxPair: #12 (s.138 NI Act notice) vs #13 (IBC s.9 application) — both drafting, hence the highest pair; still 0.09 under the ceiling

v1Control.reading: 7 of v1's 36 cost-bearing pairs exceed the same ceiling and its worst pair is 0.54 — this is the monotopicity that produced v1's false cache hits, and it is what makes the check a discriminating test rather than one everything passes.

cacheIsolation.runtimeSelfTest: Every COLD run of a cost-bearing prompt declares cacheExpectation 'expect-miss'. If any such run comes back with cost.resolution === 'semantic-cache', the prompts were NOT far enough apart on the build under test and the whole pass is VOID — no figure from it may be quoted. This is a falsification test the set applies to itself, replacing v1's untested assertion that its prompts were distinct.
cacheIsolation.warmRunsAreDeclared: Warm repeats are declared, not incidental: run 1 is cold, runs 2..N repeat the identical prompt and are EXPECTED to hit. Their cost is reported as cache benefit and never averaged into the headline.
cacheIsolation.orderingRule: Cost-bearing prompts run in ascending id, all cold runs before any warm run, so a cold run can only be contaminated by a DIFFERENT prompt (which the self-test catches) and never by its own earlier repeat.
cacheIsolation.namespaceNote: All prompts share one cache namespace (specialist:<tenant>:IN:<agentKey>) because that is what real traffic does. Isolating each prompt in its own namespace would guarantee a cold miss but would measure a configuration this platform never runs.
requiredCapture: orchestration.cacheSemanticMatch and orchestration.cacheSimilarityScore where present — a fuzzy match is exactly the case where a zero-cost answer may also be the wrong answer
cost.leafCacheHits on Queen-path runs: leaf prompt-cache hits reduce fan-out inside a request that still bills completions, and must not be reported as a free answer

harness.note: The harness defaults to v1 so an existing pass stays reproducible; v2 must be selected explicitly.
gatesThatVoidAPass: meteringVerdict METERING_REGRESSION (exit 3) — the envelope and the independent provider-log count disagree at requestId scope
separation.verdict SEPARATION_VOID (exit 5) — a cold prompt declared expect-miss was served from the semantic cache
buildChangedMidRun — the gateway image changed mid-pass, so rows describe different builds
harness.attributionModule: scripts/_nv-benchmark-attribution.mjs — reads cost.resolution (envelope) or the request-scoped 'zero-cost resolution' log line, and reports 'unattributable' rather than guessing. Tests: tests/unit/nv-benchmark-attribution.test.ts
harness.orderingIsEnforced: scripts/nv-benchmark-cost.mjs splices each runAfter prompt directly behind its predecessor. In v1 the repeat carried the next id so plain id order sufficed; item 23 here sits at the end of the file and would otherwise be dispatched many prompts later.
harness.notInstrumented: Nothing in the harness reads topicAnchors at dispatch time — they exist for the offline separation test only. The live check is the runtime self-test.

variance.unitOfVariance: distinct prompts within a class, NOT repeats of one prompt
variance.claimable: A per-class mean and standard deviation over the 3 cold runs of 3 DISTINCT prompts. n=3 is small: report the spread, and do not attach a confidence interval to it.
variance.notClaimable: Cold-to-warm spread. That is a cache effect. v1's harness already refused to average it and this set keeps that refusal explicit.
variance.v1Comparison: v1's effective sample was n=1 per class (repeats hit cache and were excluded), so no variance was claimable from it at all.

runProtocol.longContextException: long-context carries 2 prompts, not 3, and its weight is 0.02. A 2-sample spread is stated as such.

prompts.label: long context — construction arbitration fact matrix
prompts.prompt:
Review the following factual matrix and advise on entitlement, quantification and the sequence of steps. Address each head of claim separately and then their interaction.

FACTS. The claimant is the EPC contractor for a 220 kV substation package awarded by a state transmission utility. (1) The contract is a FIDIC-derived lump sum contract dated 14 March 2022 for Rs 214 crore, completion 24 months from the notice to proceed, with liquidated damages at 0.5% of contract price per week capped at 10%. (2) Site access for two of five bay locations was handed over 197 days late; the employer's engineer acknowledged the delay in monthly progress review minutes for August and September 2022 but no extension of time was ever formally granted. (3) The claimant issued notices of delay on 11 April 2022 and 2 September 2022. The contract requires notice within 28 days of the event and states that failure to notify shall render the claim time-barred. The second notice was issued 63 days after the relevant handover failure. (4) A design change instructed on 8 January 2023 increased the transformer foundation depth, adding Rs 6.4 crore of work; the employer contends it was a clarification, not a variation. (5) The employer deducted the full 10% liquidated damages cap from the fifth and sixth running account bills and encashed the performance bank guarantee for Rs 21.4 crore on 19 February 2026. (6) The claimant's programme was never approved by the engineer, and no baseline programme is annexed to the contract. The claimant's delay expert has produced an as-planned versus as-built analysis; the employer's expert relies on a time impact analysis. (7) Concurrent delay: the claimant's own subcontractor for the control building was 84 days late, overlapping the site access delay by 61 days. (8) The dispute resolution clause requires reference to the engineer, then to a dispute board, then to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act with the seat at Hyderabad. No dispute board was ever constituted. (9) The claimant issued a notice invoking arbitration on 4 March 2026.

QUESTIONS. (a) Is the extension of time claim sustainable notwithstanding the late second notice, and does the engineer's acknowledgement in the progress minutes assist? (b) How should the concurrent delay overlap be treated for entitlement to time and to money separately? (c) Is the liquidated damages deduction and the guarantee encashment open to challenge, and on what basis? (d) Does the failure to constitute the dispute board affect the arbitrability of the claims? (e) In what sequence should relief be sought, and what interim protection is available?
prompts.mustProve: Billed completions and input-token cost on a long prompt; the input side is where a long-context request differs from a short one

prompts.label: long context — pharmaceutical regulatory fact matrix
prompts.prompt:
Review the following factual matrix and advise on regulatory exposure, remediation and sequencing. Deal with each authority separately and then with the interaction between them.

FACTS. The client manufactures oral solid dosage formulations at a plant in Gujarat holding a manufacturing licence under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. (1) A routine inspection on 22 April 2026 recorded six observations, of which two were classified as critical: an unvalidated change to the blending step introduced in November 2025, and incomplete batch records for four batches of an antihypertensive tablet. (2) The state licensing authority issued a show-cause notice proposing suspension of the licence for the affected section. A reply was filed on 9 May 2026 with a corrective and preventive action plan. (3) Independently, three batches of the same product failed dissolution testing at a government laboratory, and the product was declared not of standard quality. (4) A voluntary recall of two batches was initiated on 15 May 2026, but distributor confirmations have been received for only 61% of the dispatched quantity, and the reconciliation report due within 30 days has not been filed. (5) The product is also exported. The importing country's regulator has issued an import alert citing the same blending change, and the client's overseas customer has invoked a contractual indemnity and suspended purchase orders worth USD 4.1 million. (6) Two consumer complaints alleging lack of therapeutic effect have been received; one complainant has issued a legal notice claiming compensation. (7) The label of the recalled batches understates the excipient content of one component, which the client's own investigation attributes to an artwork version control failure rather than to the blending change. (8) The qualified person who approved the unvalidated change resigned on 30 April 2026. (9) The client's insurer has been notified of a potential product liability claim but has reserved its position on coverage pending the outcome of the regulatory proceedings.

QUESTIONS. (a) What is the realistic range of regulatory outcomes on the show-cause notice and what would strengthen the reply? (b) What are the consequences of the incomplete recall reconciliation and how should it be regularised? (c) How should the labelling defect be characterised, given that it has a cause distinct from the critical observation? (d) What is the exposure on the consumer complaints and the export indemnity, and do admissions in the regulatory reply prejudice either? (e) In what sequence should the regulatory, contractual and insurance steps be taken?
prompts.mustProve: Billed completions on a second long prompt in an unrelated domain, so long-context cost is not measured from a single input

prompts.label: cache repeat — reworded statute lookup (deterministic control)
prompts.prompt: Tell me what Section 106 BNS says about death caused by a negligent act.
prompts.mustProve: Zero cost with a STATED mechanism. This probe deliberately shares its anchors with prompt 3 — it is the one place in the set where closeness is the point.
prompts.runAfterNote: Must run immediately after prompt 3 in the same pass or the measurement is meaningless.
prompts.attributionNote: A zero-cost result here is NOT self-evidently a cache hit. If the resolution comes back 'deterministic-resolver' or 'statute-fast-path', the deterministic tier answered it and the cache was never consulted, so this probe proves nothing about the cache. Only resolution 'semantic-cache' with a similarity score makes it a cache measurement. v1 could not tell these apart at all.

prompts.label: over-fire probe — strategy question wearing a section number
prompts.prompt: Devise the sequencing strategy and limitation exposure for a BNSS 482 application where a parallel PMLA proceeding is already under way.
prompts.mustProve: Must NOT be answered by the statute-FAQ fast path (NV-STATUTE-FAQ-SCOPE-001). A cost win here is a correctness FAILURE: it means a strategy question was answered with a statute excerpt.
prompts.attributionNote: This is the probe that separates a genuine deterministic win from an over-fire. Zero completions plus resolution 'deterministic-resolver' or 'statute-fast-path' on an item marked mustEscalate is the definition of deterministic-over-fire and must be reported as a quality failure, never as a saving.

prompts.label: over-fire probe — case-law research question wearing a section number
prompts.prompt: Section 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act — what have the courts held about the scope of the referral court's examination of the existence of an arbitration agreement after the 2019 amendment?
prompts.mustProve: Must escalate. A bare recitation of the section text would be an over-fire on a question that asks what the courts have held.

prompts.label: out-of-domain abstention probe
prompts.prompt: What is the recommended first-line drug and dosing schedule for stage 2 hypertension in a 62-year-old with reduced renal function?
prompts.mustProve: Must abstain or refuse. Zero cost here is correct behaviour and must be attributed as rag-abstain, not counted as a saving in any class.
prompts.attributionNote: Included so the attribution module's rag-abstain verdict is exercised by the set and not only by unit tests. An abstention must never appear in the blended cost as a cheap answer.

statute-mapping.note: weight 0 is deliberate and is the mechanism, not an omission: _nv-benchmark-cost-report.mjs blends only rows with weight > 0, so a zero weight keeps this class fully measured and printed while structurally barring it from the headline.

statute-faq.note: Same mechanism as statute-mapping. In v1 this class alone carried 0.22 of the headline at a free 100% saving.

adversarial-scope.note: Reused rather than duplicated: this is already the class for 'a reasoning question must not be taken by a fast path'. v2 adds two more members and reads the verdict from the attribution module (deterministic-over-fire) instead of inferring it from a completion count.

captured: structuredCitationCount (envelope citations[] length — NYV only; the direct baseline has no such field)
textCitationMatches (same regex both sides, so the comparison is symmetric)
cost.resolution attribution verdict per run (NEW in v2 — see cacheIsolation.requiredCapture)
notCaptured: Legal correctness. None of the above is a legal-quality score and the harness must never present one.
